key_insight: An alternating-minimization control synthesis framework can efficiently design multimode trapped-ion entangling gates while suppressing residual spin-motion entanglement, even as system size and motional complexity grow.
engineering_relevance: The method suggests that programmable, large-scale interaction patterns in trapped-ion processors may be achievable with modest control-resource growth, supporting scalable quantum hardware design.
method: Directly searches multi-tone control fields for target spin-spin interactions.
Uses alternating minimization to improve numerical stability in a high-dimensional non-convex optimization landscape.
Demonstrates both global and individually addressed gate synthesis for large ion chains.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful synthesis of all-to-all and nearest-neighbor gates for chains up to N=1000, and an individual-addressing qLDPC example at N=512, with no rapid growth in required control resources across tested regimes.
watch_item: Results are numerical and parameter-regime dependent, so experimental robustness to noise, calibration error, and hardware constraints still needs validation.
paper_title: Large-scale multimode entangling-gate synthesis in trapped-ion systems
